ko:
3Blue1Brown을
운영하고, 지금은 AI가 수학에서
en: Today, I'm chatting with Grant Sanderson, who runs 3Blue1Brown and is now working on a new project documenting the progress AI is making in math.

ko:
이뤄내고 있는 진전을 기록하는
새로운 프로젝트를 진행
en: Today, I'm chatting with Grant Sanderson, who runs 3Blue1Brown and is now working on a new project documenting the progress AI is making in math.

ko:
중인 그랜트 샌더슨과 오늘
이야기를 나눠보려고 해요.
en: Today, I'm chatting with Grant Sanderson, who runs 3Blue1Brown and is now working on a new project documenting the progress AI is making in math.

ko:
오늘 이 얘기를 나누고
싶었던 건, AI가 다른 어떤
en: I wanted to talk to you about this because AI has been making the fastest progress in mathematics out of any other field.

ko:
분야보다도 수학에서 가장 빠른
진전을 보이고 있기 때문이에요.
en: I wanted to talk to you about this because AI has been making the fastest progress in mathematics out of any other field.

ko:
여기서 무슨 일이 일어나고
있든, AI의 진전이 어떤 식으로
en: Whatever is happening here, and whatever way we're seeing AI progress happen or not happen, will tell us about what will happen to the rest of the world as AI gets better and better.

ko:
나타나거나 나타나지 않든, 그건
AI가 점점 더 좋아지면서
en: Whatever is happening here, and whatever way we're seeing AI progress happen or not happen, will tell us about what will happen to the rest of the world as AI gets better and better.

ko:
세상의 나머지 부분에서 어떤
일이 벌어질지를 말해줄 거예요.
en: Whatever is happening here, and whatever way we're seeing AI progress happen or not happen, will tell us about what will happen to the rest of the world as AI gets better and better.

ko:
3년 전 처음 인터뷰했을 때
드렸던 질문으로 시작하고 싶은데요.
en: I wanted to start with this question I asked you when I first interviewed you three years ago.

ko:
국제수학올림피아드(IMO)에서
금메달을 딸 수 있는
en: I asked you, once we have AIs that can get gold in the International Math Olympiad, wouldn't that just be AGI?

ko:
AI가 나오면, 그게 그냥
AGI 아니겠냐고 여쭤봤었죠.
en: I asked you, once we have AIs that can get gold in the International Math Olympiad, wouldn't that just be AGI?

ko:
그 문제들이 얼마나 어려운지를
생각하면, 그런 AI는 사람이
en: Wouldn't this just be able to do anything any human can do, given how hard these problems are?

ko:
할 수 있는 건 뭐든 다 할
수 있는 거 아니겠냐고요.
en: Wouldn't this just be able to do anything any human can do, given how hard these problems are?

ko:
그때 하신 답이 있었는데, 돌이켜보면
아주 현명하고 정확했더라고요.
en: You had an answer, which in retrospect turned out to be very wise and correct.

ko:
그냥 또 하나의 벤치마크가
될 거다, AI가
en: You said it'll be another benchmark, like all these other benchmarks that AI are passing.

ko:
통과해온 다른 벤치마크들처럼,
이라고 하셨죠.
en: You said it'll be another benchmark, like all these other benchmarks that AI are passing.

ko:
물론 그 이후로 AI가 전반적으로
더 좋아지긴 했지만, 이게 일어난다고
en: Obviously, AI has gotten better in a general way since then, but there won't be some "aha" moment when this happens.

ko:
해서 무슨 '아하' 하는 깨달음의
순간 같은 건 없을 거라고요.
en: Obviously, AI has gotten better in a general way since then, but there won't be some "aha" moment when this happens.

ko:
우선, 그게 왜 사실로 드러났는지에
대한 나름의 판단 근거가 궁금하고요.
en: First, I'd be curious to get your heuristics on why that turned out to be true.

ko:
두 번째로는, 이렇게 좁은
범위에서만 진전이 일어나는
en: Second, I'm curious how long you think this narrowness can continue to be true.

ko:
양상이 앞으로 얼마나 더 오래갈
거라고 보시는지 궁금해요.
en: Second, I'm curious how long you think this narrowness can continue to be true.

ko:
AI가 밀레니엄 문제 하나를
풀어낼 즈음에도, 여전히
en: By the point that AI has solved a Millennium Prize problem, do you think it's still possible that there are lots of tasks humans are doing that AI still can’t automate in the economy?

ko:
경제 안에서 사람이 하고
있는데 AI가 자동화하지
en: By the point that AI has solved a Millennium Prize problem, do you think it's still possible that there are lots of tasks humans are doing that AI still can’t automate in the economy?

ko:
못하는 일들이 많이 남아
있을 수 있다고 보세요?
en: By the point that AI has solved a Millennium Prize problem, do you think it's still possible that there are lots of tasks humans are doing that AI still can’t automate in the economy?

ko:
흥미로운 질문인 게,
해법이 어떤 모습일지
en: It's an interesting question because it's hard to answer without knowing what the solution looks like ahead of time.

ko: 미리 알지 못하면 답하기가 어렵거든요.
en: It's an interesting question because it's hard to answer without knowing what the solution looks like ahead of time.

ko:
IMO를 예로 들면, 3년 전
질문의 핵심은 이 문제들 중 일부의
en: If we take the IMO, the spirit of your question three years ago was in looking at how some of the solutions to these problems really seem to require creativity.

ko:
풀이가 정말 창의성을 요구하는
것처럼 보인다는 데 있었잖아요.
en: If we take the IMO, the spirit of your question three years ago was in looking at how some of the solutions to these problems really seem to require creativity.

ko:
이 문제를 출제하는 사람들은
그렇게 쉽게 훈련으로
en: The designers of these problems try to come up with things that you can't train for as easily.

ko:
대비할 수 없는 걸
만들어내려고 하거든요.
en: The designers of these problems try to come up with things that you can't train for as easily.

ko:
근데 IMO의 지저분한
비밀은, 사실 그중
en: The dirty secret with the IMO is that you really can train for a lot of them.

ko: 상당수는 훈련으로 대비가 된다는 거예요.
en: The dirty secret with the IMO is that you really can train for a lot of them.

ko:
지금 한창 진행 중인 AI와 수학
프로젝트 전체를 놓고 보면, 말씀하신
en: With the whole AI and math project underway, as you point out, one of the reasons it's interesting at all is that there's a spiky frontier to AI, and math is just right there in one of the spikes.

ko:
대로 이게 애초에 흥미로운 이유 중
하나가, AI의 최전선이 들쭉날쭉하다는
en: With the whole AI and math project underway, as you point out, one of the reasons it's interesting at all is that there's a spiky frontier to AI, and math is just right there in one of the spikes.

ko:
건데, 수학이 바로 그 뾰족 솟은
부분 중 하나에 있다는 거예요.
en: With the whole AI and math project underway, as you point out, one of the reasons it's interesting at all is that there's a spiky frontier to AI, and math is just right there in one of the spikes.

ko:
그런데 그 들쭉날쭉함에는 프랙탈적인
성질이 있어요. 수학 안에서 구체적인
en: But there's a fractal nature to that spikiness, because when you zoom into the specific progress within math, you have some things that are a lot easier than others.

ko:
진전을 확대해서 들여다보면, 어떤
부분은 다른 부분보다 훨씬 쉽거든요.
en: But there's a fractal nature to that spikiness, because when you zoom into the specific progress within math, you have some things that are a lot easier than others.

ko:
IMO만 놓고 보면, 사실
이제는 옛날 얘기죠.
en: If we just think about IMO, which is old news at this point.

ko:
AI가 정말 잘하기 시작한
지 벌써 2년이 됐으니까요.
en: It's been two years since they're really doing quite well.

ko:
다음 이유만 아니었다면 2024년에
금메달을 땄을 거예요.
en: They would have gotten a gold in 2024 if not for the following reason.

ko: 정말 잘해요.
en: They're very good.

ko:
기하 문제는 그냥 단숨에 풀어버렸다고
봐야 해요, 기본적으로.
en: They just cold-solved geometry basically.

ko:
IMO에는 기하,
정수론, 대수, 조합론,
en: The IMO has these four categories of problems: geometry, number theory, algebra, and combinatorics.

ko: 이렇게 네 가지 문제 범주가 있어요.
en: The IMO has these four categories of problems: geometry, number theory, algebra, and combinatorics.

ko:
기하는 2024년
이후로 그냥 19초 만에
en: Geometry, it just solves it in nineteen seconds since 2024 because it's a brute force solver.

ko:
풀어버려요, 무작정 대입해서
푸는 solver니까요.
en: Geometry, it just solves it in nineteen seconds since 2024 because it's a brute force solver.

ko:
솔직히 까놓고 말하면,
학생들도 그런 문제에
en: The dirty secret is that for students, there's also a brute force way you can go at it.

ko:
무작정 대입으로 밀어붙이는
방법이 있긴 해요.
en: The dirty secret is that for students, there's also a brute force way you can go at it.

ko:
조합론이 변수예요. 훨씬 더 장난스럽고
퍼즐처럼 보이는 문제들이거든요.
en: Combinatorics is the wild card: much more playful, puzzly-seeming problems.

ko:
그 해 시험엔 조합론 문제가 두 개
있었는데, 항상 그런 건 아니에요.
en: There were two combinatorics problems on that year's test, and there's not always.

ko:
카테고리가 네 개,
문제가 여섯 개니까, 어느
en: There are four categories and six different problems, so it's a toss-up which one is going to have two questions.

ko:
카테고리가 두 문제씩
차지할지는 반반이에요.
en: There are four categories and six different problems, so it's a toss-up which one is going to have two questions.

ko:
그 해에 기하 문제가 더
많았다면 금메달을 땄을 거예요.
en: Had it been more geometry questions, they would have gotten a gold that year.

ko:
그런데 그 조합론 문제들
앞에서는 고전해요.
en: But it struggles on those combinatorics ones.

ko:
수학이 인류에게 남은 마지막 보루라는
횃불을 지키고 싶은 사람이라면,
en: Someone who's trying to keep that torch of the last holdout of math for humanity might say those are the ones that require more creativity.

ko:
저런 문제들이야말로 더 많은 창의성을
요구한다고 말할 수도 있어요.
en: Someone who's trying to keep that torch of the last holdout of math for humanity might say those are the ones that require more creativity.

ko:
그렇다 해도, 질문의 요지 —
밀레니엄 문제를 푼다면 그게
en: Even then, the spirit of your question—if they're solving a Millennium Prize problem, does that also service a lot of white-collar work?—suggests that whatever the rate limiter is between where we are now and that is the same as the rate limiter for making things better at white-collar work.

ko:
화이트칼라 업무 전반에도 도움이
되는 거냐는 — 를 생각해보면,
en: Even then, the spirit of your question—if they're solving a Millennium Prize problem, does that also service a lot of white-collar work?—suggests that whatever the rate limiter is between where we are now and that is the same as the rate limiter for making things better at white-collar work.

ko:
결국 지금 여기서 거기까지 가는
걸 가로막는 병목이 화이트칼라
en: Even then, the spirit of your question—if they're solving a Millennium Prize problem, does that also service a lot of white-collar work?—suggests that whatever the rate limiter is between where we are now and that is the same as the rate limiter for making things better at white-collar work.

ko:
업무를 더 잘하게 만드는
병목과 똑같다는 뜻이 돼요.
en: Even then, the spirit of your question—if they're solving a Millennium Prize problem, does that also service a lot of white-collar work?—suggests that whatever the rate limiter is between where we are now and that is the same as the rate limiter for making things better at white-collar work.

ko:
그림을 몇 가지 다르게
그려볼 수 있을 것 같아요.
en: We could paint a couple of different ways.

ko:
리만 가설에 초점을 맞춰본다면,
그걸 푼다는 게 어떤 모습일까요?
en: If we focus on the Riemann hypothesis, what would it look like to solve that?

ko:
이런 모델들은 특정 지식 영역
하나를 정말 깊이 아는 데 탁월하고,
en: These things are extremely good at a specific domain of knowledge, knowing it very deeply, and then knowing another domain, and another.

ko:
그다음 또 다른 영역, 또 다른
영역까지 아주 잘 알아요.
en: These things are extremely good at a specific domain of knowledge, knowing it very deeply, and then knowing another domain, and another.

ko: 이건 이미 지적하신 적 있잖아요.
en: You've pointed this out.

ko:
이렇게 초인적으로 폭넓게 모든 분야를
그렇게 잘 아는 무언가가, 정작
en: It's bizarre to have something with this superhuman breadth that knows all the fields so well, and yet isn't finding those lightning bolts that connect them.

ko:
그 분야들을 이어주는 번개 같은
통찰은 찾아내지 못한다는 게 이상해요.
en: It's bizarre to have something with this superhuman breadth that knows all the fields so well, and yet isn't finding those lightning bolts that connect them.

ko:
제 생각엔 이게 실제로 자기가
전문인 분야들 사이에서 연결점을
en: I think we're starting to see sparks of it actually finding connections between the things it's an expert at.

ko:
찾아내는 스파크가 조금씩
보이기 시작하는 것 같아요.
en: I think we're starting to see sparks of it actually finding connections between the things it's an expert at.

ko: 이건 이따가 분명 얘기하게 될 거예요.
en: I'm sure we'll talk about it.

ko:
리만 가설의 해법이 그런 성격의
것이라면, 그건 화이트칼라
en: If the nature of the solution to the Riemann hypothesis was something like that, that feels pretty distinct to me from what's necessary to get good at white-collar work.

ko:
업무를 잘하는 데 필요한
것과는 저한테 꽤 달라 보여요.
en: If the nature of the solution to the Riemann hypothesis was something like that, that feels pretty distinct to me from what's necessary to get good at white-collar work.

ko:
그리고 실제로 그게 해법의 성격일 수도
있다고 믿을 만한 이유가 있어요.
en: And there's a reason to believe that might be the nature of the solution.

ko:
휴 몽고메리와 프리먼 다이슨이
고등연구소(IAS)에서
en: I don't know if you know the story of Hugh Montgomery and Freeman Dyson at the IAS.

ko: 있었던 이야기를 아시는지 모르겠네요.
en: I don't know if you know the story of Hugh Montgomery and Freeman Dyson at the IAS.

ko: 좀 곁가지이긴 한데, 재밌는 이야기예요.
en: This is a side tangent, but it's a fun story.

ko:
점심 자리였는지 뭐였는지는 모르겠지만,
리만 제타 함수의 영점 쌍들
en: I don't know if it was over lunch or something like that, but you have this number theorist who is just trying to understand the statistical correlation between pairs of zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

ko:
사이의 통계적 상관관계를 이해하려던
한 정수론학자가 있었어요.
en: I don't know if it was over lunch or something like that, but you have this number theorist who is just trying to understand the statistical correlation between pairs of zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

ko:
리만 가설은 결국 이
영점들이 전부 하나의
en: The Riemann hypothesis is all about whether all these zeros sit on a straight line.

ko: 직선 위에 놓여 있는지에 관한 거예요.
en: The Riemann hypothesis is all about whether all these zeros sit on a straight line.

ko: 그가 던져볼 수 있는 정량적인 질문
en: He finds this quantitative question you could ask, and he writes down a formula.

ko:
하나를 찾아냈고,
공식을 하나 적어냈어요.
en: He finds this quantitative question you could ask, and he writes down a formula.

ko: 사인 제곱분의 1 같은 모양이었어요.
en: It looks like one over sine squared or something like that.

ko:
물리학자인 프리먼 다이슨이 그러는
거예요. "나 그 식 아는데."
en: Freeman Dyson, a physicist, is like, "I know that expression.

ko:
"그거 무작위 에르미트 행렬의 고유값을
연구할 때 나오는 식이거든요"라고
en: That expression comes up in studying the eigenvalues for random Hermitian matrices," which was something that comes up in studying the energy levels of a nucleus.

ko:
했는데, 그건 원자핵의 에너지
준위를 연구할 때 나오는 것이었어요.
en: That expression comes up in studying the eigenvalues for random Hermitian matrices," which was something that comes up in studying the energy levels of a nucleus.

ko:
겉보기에는 전혀 다른 두
가지의 통계적 성질이 사실
en: The idea that the statistics of those two seemingly different things were the same prompted an exploration of whether there are aspects of random matrix theory that might be relevant to the Riemann zeta function.

ko:
똑같다는 이 발상이, 랜덤
행렬 이론의 어떤 측면이 리만
en: The idea that the statistics of those two seemingly different things were the same prompted an exploration of whether there are aspects of random matrix theory that might be relevant to the Riemann zeta function.

ko:
제타 함수와 관련 있을 수도
있다는 탐구로 이어졌어요.
en: The idea that the statistics of those two seemingly different things were the same prompted an exploration of whether there are aspects of random matrix theory that might be relevant to the Riemann zeta function.

ko:
거기서 정말 뭔가 결실을
얻을 수 있을지는,
en: I think it's a little bit of an open question whether there is fruit to be had there.

ko:
저는 아직 좀 열려
있는 질문이라고 봐요.
en: I think it's a little bit of an open question whether there is fruit to be had there.

ko:
그런데 이렇게 서로 다른 두
분야를 잇는 것—만약 리만 가설의
en: But that bridging together of two different fields—if it turned out that the solution to the Riemann hypothesis was exploring an idea like that even further—has the character of how you expect LLMs to be good at math.

ko:
해법이 바로 이런 아이디어를 더
파고드는 거였다면—그건 LLM이
en: But that bridging together of two different fields—if it turned out that the solution to the Riemann hypothesis was exploring an idea like that even further—has the character of how you expect LLMs to be good at math.

ko:
수학을 잘할 거라고 기대할 법한
바로 그런 성격을 띠고 있어요.
en: But that bridging together of two different fields—if it turned out that the solution to the Riemann hypothesis was exploring an idea like that even further—has the character of how you expect LLMs to be good at math.

ko: LLM은 양자물리학 전문가고요.
en: They're experts at quantum physics.

ko: 해석적 수론에도 전문가예요.
en: They're experts at analytic number theory.

ko:
몽고메리와 다이슨이 우연히
점심을 먹다가 그 얘기를 나눌
en: They should be able to see that similarity in a way that doesn't require Montgomery and Dyson to be having lunch and happen to talk about it.

ko:
필요 없이도, 그런 유사성을
알아볼 수 있어야 하죠.
en: They should be able to see that similarity in a way that doesn't require Montgomery and Dyson to be having lunch and happen to talk about it.

ko:
그건 화이트칼라 업무랑은
완전히 다른 거예요.
en: That's totally different from white-collar work.

ko:
